Application Materials.content:
- We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained. Please send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** the originals.
- If you are not a national of a [majority English-speaking country](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/) you will need to submit evidence of your proficiency in English to the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) and University's required standards.
- One completed reference: Please check whether one or two references are required for the programme for which you are applying. You should supply at least one reference from an academic referee who is in a position to comment on the standard of your academic work and suitability for postgraduate level study. Where this is not possible, references from other sources that provide evidence of your ability to undertake postgraduate study and suitability for your chosen programme will be accepted; references from family members, partners or spouses cannot be accepted.
- References for Postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If your reference is coming direct from your referee, it must come direct from their institutional or company email address and can be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk), along with your student reference number, name and programme of study.
- Not all programmes require a personal statement; however, if provided, it should be tailored to the particular course. Admissions tutors will be looking for an explanation of how the course links your past and future, an insight into your abilities and fit with the course, evidence of your skills, commitment and enthusiasm, reasons why you want to study this course at the University of Exeter, and your particular interest in the subject.
- Personal statement guidance: **Stick to under 500 words in length**; keep sentences short and clear; consider using headings such as 'Why the University of Exeter?' 'Why this course?' 'Career plans’; proofread; check grammar, punctuation and spelling; and use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
- As a **minimum** to enable an initial decision on taught programme applications, applicants need to complete the Module Information section of the application form giving details of any outstanding modules and expected date of completion, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application.
- We recommend uploading all supporting documents with your application. You can apply before completing all academic qualifications, but you will need to provide any interim transcripts that you have to support your application.
- International students: original copies are not required at the application stage and the University would not recommend sending these during the application process.

Interview Requirements.content: We may require you to attend an interview before we issue you with your CAS. If you are required to attend an interview, we will send you an email with details of the time and date and joining instructions. The meeting will take place via Microsoft Teams. The purpose of the Pre-CAS interview is to assess that an applicant has a genuine intent to study at the University of Exeter, it is not to assess academic abilities. Attendance at an interview is mandatory and we will be unable to issue a CAS until the interview has taken place. Applicants required to attend a Pre-CAS interview will be sent further details once they have an unconditional place and where applicable a deposit has been paid.

Application Deadlines.content: **January start date:** applications to apply for programmes that start in January 2027 will open on **Monday 2 March 2026** and close at **23:59 Monday 4 January 2027**. View a list of [programmes with a January 2027 start](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/january-start/).

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A 2:2 or equivalent** from a recognised university, including **at least one mathematical / quantitative module at 2:2 or equivalent**.
- The University considers applications where there is evidence of exceptional performance in modules relevant to the programme of study, **significant relevant work experience or professional qualifications**.
- For students from China: applicants to postgraduate taught Masters courses need a bachelor’s degree certificate and graduation certificate from a domestic university recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education, with grades equivalent to the UK **2:1 or 2:2** requirement depending on the course.
- For 2026 entry postgraduate taught China grade equivalency: **2:2 = 70%**; **2:1 = 75%**.
- For China: the previous domestic university ranking requirement has been removed; all Chinese universities use a unified score standard for assessment, and all undergraduate institutions on the official recognised list of the Chinese Ministry of Education are accepted. Some courses may have additional undergraduate subject background requirements.

Program Overview.content:
MSc Business Analytics is a **1 year full-time** programme offered at **Streatham Campus**, with a January start option. The programme runs from September to September or **January to January** depending on your chosen start month.
The programme is for students interested in a career related to business analytics or who wish to study a related PhD. Students learn how to support managers to make data driven decisions using techniques including analysis of social media and marketing data, optimisation and forecasting. The course provides foundations in business analytics, basic programming and mathematical skills, alongside techniques to present and communicate data to managers.
The programme is inspired by global challenges and draws on the University of Exeter’s environmental research, including business challenges around climate exposure in supply chains and investment portfolios, climate change and natural hazards risk, and wider environmental impacts. Optional study areas allow students to flex the programme to suit their interests and career or research aspirations, including areas such as Marketing Analytics, Strategic & HR Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Environmental Analytics.
Students complete a research project / Business Project supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department, based around a sizeable business problem that draws on their business analytics skills. The programme is delivered over three terms and is University-based throughout; taught components are delivered in the first two terms, with the third term used to complete the Business Project.
Teaching and learning include lectures, workshops, practical sessions, practitioner insight seminars, private study, case study development, group work, individual projects, and collaboration with industry partners. Assessment includes practical exercises, project work, written assignments, presentations, multiple-choice tests, and examinations.
The University has invested £50 million in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence capabilities through the Accelerating Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (ADA) project, which has invested in teaching, research and infrastructure that benefits this programme. Students are taught by internationally respected academics, and the programme is embedded within the [Operations and Analytics group](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/management/about/operations-analytics/) in the Department of Management. The [Centre for Simulation and Analytics Management](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/centres/csam/) supports research and teaching within the programme, focusing on analytical modelling and computer simulation to address real-world problems.
The programme has links with professional organisations such as the Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM) and the Chartered Institute of Personnel Development (CIPD), enriching the programme with industry insights and aligning the curriculum with professional standards and real-world needs.
The QS Business Master’s Ranking 2025: Business Analytics ranks Exeter’s MSc Business Analytics **26th globally** within the Diversity Indicator Group and **top 90 globally** for Employability. Graduates can pursue roles including Business Consultant, Data Consultant, Business Analyst, Supply Chain Analyst, Marketing Analyst, HR Analyst, and Business Manager, with opportunities in consulting, tech, finance, procurement, HR, marketing, public sector and third sector organisations, as well as Graduate Management schemes.
High achieving students may apply for the [QTEM Programme](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroad/pgstudyabroad/qtem/). If accepted, students spend an additional semester studying at one of QTEM’s academic partners, followed by a quantitatively focused internship and participation in the [QTEM Data Challenge](https://www.qtem.org/en/students/data-challenge/1), which includes online data science and leadership courses and real data analysis.

Curriculum.content:
Duration: **1 year full time**. Entry year: **2026 + January 2027 start**. Campus: **Streatham Campus**.
The programme is delivered over **three terms** and is **University-based throughout this time**. The taught components of the programme are delivered in the first two terms, leaving the third term to complete the **Business Project**. The programme runs from **September to September or January to January** depending on your chosen start month.
During the programme you will study modules totalling **180 credits**: **120 credits of compulsory modules** and **60 credits of optional modules**.
Compulsory modules:
| Code | Module | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BEMM457 | Topics in Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM458 | Programming for Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM459 | Database Technologies for Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM460 | Statistics and Mathematics for Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM461 | Analytics and Visualisation for Managers and Consultants | 15 |
| BEMM828 | MSc Project | 45 |
Optional modules:
| Code | Module | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BEMM394 | Entrepreneurship: New Venture Creation | 15 |
| BEMM462 | Operations Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM463 | Marketing Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM464 | Strategic and HR Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM465 | Environmental Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM783 | Supply Chain Analytics | 15 |
| COM2019 | Programming for Prompt Engineering | 15 |
| SSIM916 | Machine Learning for Social Data Science | 15 |
You will complete a research project (**Business Project**) supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department. Your project will be based around a sizeable business problem that draws upon your newly developed business analytics skills.
High achieving students have the opportunity to apply for the [Quantitative Techniques for Economics and Management (QTEM) programme](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroad/pgstudyabroad/qtem/), which includes an additional semester studying at one of the prestigious academic partners, followed by a quantitatively focussed internship and participation in the [QTEM Data Challenge](https://www.qtem.org/en/students/data-challenge/1).

Cost of Attendance.content:
We estimate a single student living in Exeter or Cornwall will need approximately **£1,300-£2,000 a month** to meet basic living expenses such as accommodation (rent), transport, food and drink, entertainment, utility bills, clothes and socialising.
| Expense | Average cost per week* |
| --- | --- |
| Student halls (bills included) | £150-£270 (self-catered)£250-£345 (catered) |
| Rooms in private accommodation (without bills) | £135-£250 |
| Household bills (gas, electricity, water, broadband & a TV licence) | £30 |
| Groceries | £60 |
| Socialising (dining out, going to cafes & bars) | £40 |
| Public transport | £18 |
| Mobile phone bill (SIM only plan) | £4.50 |
| Student gym membership | £15 |
| **Total** | **£316 - £421/week estimate** |
*Based on average local spend April 2026.
As an approximate estimate for a single person living in shared accommodation expect to pay at least these amounts **per month**: gas £55 - £75, electricity £65-£85, internet £25 - £35, water £30-£40. TV licences are mandatory for everyone who views content in any format, including on-demand such as BBC iPlayer. Costs £13.25 per month.

Financial Aid.content:
Exeter Excellence Scholarships 2026/27 - Postgraduate Taught (Masters), **Round 4 - January 2027 entry only**, are available for eligible campus-based Masters programmes including [MSc Business Analytics](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/courses/business/business_analytics/). Awards are **£3,000, £5,000 or £10,000** to help cover the costs of studying at the University of Exeter.
Eligibility:
- Applicants must have International fee status, including EU applicants required to pay International fees in 2026/27.
- Applicants must already hold an offer, conditional or unconditional, to study an eligible Postgraduate taught degree at the University of Exeter, beginning in **January 2027**.
- Applicants must not have applied in Round 1 or 2 of the 2026/27 Exeter Excellence scholarship scheme for September 2026 entry for the same programme.
Selection is based on academic merit and the application process. Applicants will typically be expected to demonstrate that they have achieved or are able to achieve the equivalent of UK upper second class degree (2:1), and must demonstrate academic and career ambitions, a clear plan for making the most of the study opportunity, social responsibility, and willingness to engage with the Exeter community.
To be considered, once applicants have their programme offer, they should apply using the webform [here](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/4vjgYKQZb1). A personal statement of no more than 300 words is required. **Round 4 - January 2027 entry only closes on Thursday 26 November 2026. Round 4 notifications will be sent out within one month on a rolling basis and no later than Thursday 10 December 2026.**
These scholarships are awarded as a reduction in the first-year International tuition fees. They are not recurrent for subsequent years of study. They can be combined with a University of Exeter Postgraduate Taught Scholarship 2026/27 for Bangladesh, Canada, China (mainland), India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Nepal, Pakistan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand, Türkiye or Vietnam to a maximum award value of **£10,000**. Full Terms and Conditions are available [here](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/v8media/universityofexeter/funding/documents/Important-info-TsCs-Exeter-Excellence-PGT-2026-27.pdf).
| Application deadline: | 26th November 2026 |
|---|---|
| Value: | £3,000, £5,000 or £10,000 first year tuition fees discount |
| Duration of award: | for 1 year |
| Contact: Admissions Scholarships | [admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk) |

Multiple Applications.content: No. When you accept your place on a programme you are committing to that specific programme. Any other offers you may be holding will be released.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Requests for deferral will be considered on a case by case basis. Applicants wishing to defer will need to put their request in writing and [submit it via our enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/) (please ensure you quote your Exeter Reference Number – which can be found on the top of your original offer email). We aim to notify applicants of an outcome within **10 working days**. Applicants are only permitted to defer entry once. Subsequent to this, a new application will be required which will be considered in line with others applying for entry in that year.
| Start date | Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| All other start dates | **Within 4 weeks of the start date of your programme** |
Applicants who do not request a deferral within this timeframe will be required to reapply, as your original application and documentation will not be retained.
